title: Report what a worker thread threw

blocks.text: An exception thrown out of a thread's `run()` ends **that** thread. It never reaches the thread that called `start()`: it goes to the thread's `UncaughtExceptionHandler`, and with none set it is only printed to `System.err`, "silently lost" from the application's point of view. The page's advice is to always set a handler.

Write `Crash.runAndReport(String name, Runnable task)`. Run `task` on a new thread named `name`, wait for that thread to finish, and return what it threw as `"<thread name>: <message>"`, or `null` if it finished normally. Anything the task throws counts, `Error`s included.

cases.says: A RuntimeException thrown by the task comes back as "name: message"; a task that finishes gives null.
An Error thrown by the task is reported the same way.
The task runs on a new thread with the given name, not on the caller.

concepts: An exception thrown from run() ends that thread and goes to its UncaughtExceptionHandler, never to the thread that called start().
